years.retained_earnings_note: Retained earnings for Wirecard uses total shareholders' equity as a proxy -- the actual retained-earnings sub-line wasn't separately extractable. This makes the Altman Z''-Score slightly OPTIMISTIC relative to the true figure, since total equity also includes share capital, share premium and other reserves and so typically exceeds retained earnings. Disclosed here as a limitation, not corrected silently.
years.source: [EUR] https://www.wirecard.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Annual-Report-2016.pdf | Consolidated income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement, Annual Report FY2016. Originally reported in kEUR, converted to EUR millions (divide by 1000) for consistency with other companies. EBIT = 235,188 kEUR (post amortisation/depreciation incl. M&A-related). Total Debt = non-current interest-bearing liabilities (579,475) + current interest-bearing liabilities (15,066) = 594,541 kEUR. Receivables = "Trade and other receivables" only (190,185 kEUR); EXCLUDES a separate balance sheet line "Receivables of acquiring business" (402,423 kEUR) which is roughly double trade receivables and is the line item later central to the fraud investigation (fabricated cash/receivables were traced to the third-party acquiring business). Flagged for discussion in write-up: honest ratio analysis using only standard "trade receivables" would have missed this. NOTE: as-filed figures, later found materially fraudulent -- this project tests whether AS-FILED numbers showed honest distress signals, not whether fraud was detectable (AuditIQ's remit).

years.source: [EUR] https://wirecard.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Annual-Report-2017.pdf | Consolidated income statement, statement of financial position, cash flow statement, Annual Report FY2017. Converted kEUR to EUR millions. Total Debt = non-current interest-bearing liabilities (754,792) + current interest-bearing liabilities (311,611) = 1,066,403 kEUR. Receivables = "Trade and other receivables" only (269,669 kEUR); EXCLUDES "Receivables of the acquiring business" (442,012 kEUR), consistent with FY2016 treatment. FLAG: Revenue grew 44.9% YoY but Receivables of acquiring business grew only 9.8% (402,423 -> 442,012) -- divergence worth noting though not conclusive on its own. Total Debt roughly doubled YoY, mostly via non-current interest-bearing liabilities. As-filed figures, later found materially fraudulent.

years.source: [EUR] https://wirecard.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Annual-Report-2018.pdf | Consolidated statement of financial position, income statement, cash flow statement, Annual Report FY2018 (reported directly in EUR millions, no conversion needed). Total Debt = non-current interest-bearing liabilities (1,348.7) + current interest-bearing liabilities (117.4) = 1,466.1. Receivables = "Trade and other receivables" only (357.4); EXCLUDES "Receivables of the acquiring business" (684.9), consistent with FY2016-17 treatment. MAJOR RED FLAG: Cash flow statement shows "Change in receivables" of -344.9m in 2018 vs -99.2m in 2017 (3.5x worse), while revenue only grew 35.4% -- a sharp divergence between rising reported EBIT/net income and actual cash conversion. Receivables of acquiring business grew 55% (442.0 -> 684.9) outpacing revenue growth. This earnings-quality gap (profit growing faster than cash) is a strong honest-distress signal independent of the later-confirmed fraud. As-filed figures, later found materially fraudulent -- FY2019 never received an audited report (see companies.py notes) and is treated as the failure event, not a data year.
